issues.legal_issue: A tenant in an eviction proceeding pending when the new rent law commenced could obtain transitional protection only by making the required deposit within the statutory period, not by depositing after a newly constructed building’s temporary exemption expired.
material_facts: The building was completed and let before the new rent law commenced, and the former rent law did not apply to it.
The landlord’s eviction suit was filed before the new law commenced and remained pending when it commenced.

The tenant made the required deposit after the building’s ten-year exemption had expired, rather than within one month of commencement of the new law or, if later, of learning that the suit was pending.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was not entitled to transitional protection because the deposit was not made within the period specified by the transitional provision; the judgments granting that protection were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 39 and 40 of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, transitional protection requires a qualifying eviction suit, appeal, or revision to have been pending when the Act commenced and the tenant to have deposited the required rent, damages, interest, and costs within one month of commencement or, if later, knowledge of the proceeding. The reference to commencement means commencement of the Act, not expiry of the ten-year exemption under Section 2(2). Where the conditions are met, eviction protection is subject to the exceptions stated in Section 39 by reference to Section 20. The Court relied on Om Prakash Gupta v. Dig Vijendrapal Gupta, Nand Kishore Marwah v. Samundri Devi, Atma Ram Mittal v. Ishwar Singh Punia, and Ram Swaroop Rai v. Lilavathi, and rejected the contrary approach in Vineet Kumar v. Mangal Sain Wadhera.

predicates.pre_commencement_eviction_proceeding_pen: An eviction suit, or an appeal or revision arising from such a suit, concerning a building to which the former rent law did not apply was pending when the new rent law commenced.
predicates.qualifying_newly_regulated_building: The building was temporarily exempt from rent regulation as a newly constructed building and became subject to the new law after that temporary exemption ended.
predicates.deposit_outside_initial_window: The tenant made the required deposit later than one month after commencement of the new law or, if later, later than one month after learning that the proceeding was pending.

issues.definition: When a qualifying eviction proceeding was pending at commencement and the tenant deposited outside the initial statutory window, the tenant is denied transitional protection.
